text: Every one of us began as a single cell, about a tenth of a millimeter wide. How does one tiny cell start a whole new life? The answer is the reproductive system. Let's follow the journey.
The female reproductive system includes two ovaries, two fallopian tubes, the uterus and the cervix. The ovaries hold the eggs, and they make the hormones estrogen and progesterone.

A baby girl is born with all the eggs she will ever have, around one to two million. About once a month, usually one egg matures inside a fluid-filled sac called a follicle. At ovulation, the follicle bursts and releases it. The finger-like ends of the fallopian tube, called fimbriae, sweep the egg inside. In a whole lifetime, only a few hundred eggs are ever released.

Now the male system. The testes make sperm and the hormone testosterone. Sperm form inside tightly coiled tubes called seminiferous tubules, then mature in the epididymis, and travel through the vas deferens. The testes sit outside the body because sperm develop best a little cooler than body temperature. Millions of sperm are made every day.

Fertilization usually happens in the fallopian tube. Many sperm can reach the egg, but normally only one gets inside. Then the egg's outer layer changes and blocks all the others. The egg and the sperm each carry twenty-three chromosomes. Together, they make forty-six, a brand new set of instructions.

The fertilized egg divides again and again as it travels toward the uterus. After several days it becomes a hollow ball of cells called a blastocyst. About six to ten days after fertilization, it burrows into the thick, blood-rich lining of the uterus. This is called implantation, and it is where pregnancy begins.
And if no egg is fertilized? Hormone levels fall, and the uterine lining sheds. That is the menstrual period. Then the cycle starts again.
See a doctor for very painful or irregular periods, a lump or pain in a testicle, or trouble getting pregnant after a year of trying, or six months if you are over thirty-five.

Remember three things. Ovaries release eggs, and testes make sperm. Fertilization happens in the fallopian tube. And the embryo implants in the lining of the uterus. Next time, a new body story unfolds.
